[LSIG.1.4.2] The denominator is `min(W, elapsed)`, never the full window `W`.
During the first `W` of an instance's life less than `W` of history exists, so
dividing by `W` would under-report; `min(W, elapsed)` removes that warm-up
bias. While `elapsed` is `0`, `onset_rate` is `0`.

tla.name: lsig_1_4_2__denominator_is_elapsed_before_W
tla.note: THE DENOMINATOR IS ELAPSED BEFORE W, within the scope: at a read after the first absorption it is 0 while no time has elapsed since `t_first`, the elapsed time until W of it has passed, and W from then on; the full window from the first sample is refused (`.teeth.full_window`) and the warm-up correction is seen (`.probe.warmup`). Less than the clause: the denominator's shape alone. The edge count N+ and the quotient are not computed here; the value is the clause-literal references'.
